judge_response:
ANALYSIS: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) is a functional gastrointestinal disorder subclassified based on predominant stool pattern: IBS-D (diarrhea-predominant), IBS-C (constipation-predominant), IBS-M (mixed), or IBS-U (unsubtyped). The predicted diagnosis specifies "Irritable Bowel Syndrome, diarrhea-predominant (IBS-D)", which is a valid, clinically meaningful refinement of the broader reference diagnosis. This subtyping aligns with Rome IV criteria and guides management (e.g., loperamide, rifaximin, or eluxadoline for IBS-D). As long as the clinical presentation supports diarrhea predominance (e.g., >25% of stools are loose/watery, <25% are hard/lumpy), this specification is accurate and appropriate.

VERDICT: CORRECT
